                                 OPERATING AGREEMENT

                                                OF

                      GREENWOOD OPERATIONS HOLDINGS LLC

       THIS OPERATING AGREEMENT of GREENWOOD OPERATIONS HOLDINGS
LLC (“Company”), dated as of September 26, 2025 (this “Agreement”), is made by and among is
made by and among the undersigned members (each, a “Member” and collectively, the
“Members”) and the Company. All capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall
have the meanings provided in Exhibit A attached hereto.

       WHEREAS:

       A.      The Company was formed as a New Jersey limited liability company, pursuant to
the New Jersey Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act (the “Act”), for the purposes,
and on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement;

       B.      The Members desire to enter into this Agreement, which Agreement shall supersede
any and all previous agreements, to define and express the terms and conditions relating to the
governance of the Company and the Members’ respective rights and obligations with respect to
the Company.

       NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein
contained and other good and valuable consideration, the sufficiency of which is hereby
acknowledged, the parties agree that this Agreement shall govern the relationship of the Members
among themselves and with the Company, as follows:

                                             Article I
                                            Formation

       Section 1.1.    Formation and Name.

                (a)     The Company was formed as a New Jersey limited liability company under
the name GREENWOOD OPERATIONS HOLDINGS LLC. Upon formation of the Company,
a certificate of formation (the “Certificate”) was filed, pursuant to and in accordance with the
provisions of the Act, in the office of the New Jersey Department of the Treasury, Division of
Revenue and Enterprise Services. The Members hereby make and execute this Agreement to set
forth the rights, duties, obligations and limitations on the liabilities of the Members, including,
without limitation, the rights of the Members with respect to the assets and profits of the Company,
which the Members shall be entitled to receive by reason of being members of the Company.

                (b)    The Company shall comply with all requirements necessary to qualify the
Company as a foreign limited liability company in each other jurisdiction in which foreign
qualification of the Company is either necessary or appropriate.



                                               -1-

===== PAGE 206 =====
                 (c)    Each Member shall execute, acknowledge and deliver all certificates and
other instruments conforming to this Agreement that are reasonably necessary or appropriate to
qualify, or, as appropriate, to continue or terminate any qualification of, the Company as a foreign
limited liability company in all jurisdictions in which the Company may conduct business.

       Section 1.2. Principal Office. The principal office of the Company shall be located at
such place as the Manager shall determine from time to time.

        Section 1.3. Registered Office and Agent. The name and address of the Company’s
registered agent shall be as indicated in the Certificate. Such office and agent may be changed,
from time to time, as the Manager shall determine.

       Section 1.4.    Purposes. The business of the Company shall be solely for the purpose of
engaging in:

            (a)        the acquisition and ownership of certain membership interest in the
Greenwood Opco;

               (b)     undertaking such other activities incident or appropriate to the foregoing;
and

               (c)     engaging in any other lawful act or activity permitted by the Act, that are
related or incidental to and necessary, convenient or advisable for the accomplishment of the
above-mentioned purposes.

        Section 1.5. Duration of the Company. The term of the Company commenced upon the
filing of the Certificate, and shall continue in perpetuity unless terminated in accordance with
Article X.

       Section 1.6.    Rights, Obligations and Exculpation.

                (a)      The Members shall have no liability under this Agreement or otherwise with
respect to the debts, liabilities, expenses and other obligations of the Company solely by reason of
their capacity as Members, except to the extent provided in the Act and in this Agreement.

               (b)      None of the Members shall have the power to bind the other Members,
except as specifically provided in this Agreement. None of the Members or the Company shall be
responsible or liable for any indebtedness, liability, expense or other obligation of any other
Member incurred, either prior to or following the execution of this Agreement, except that the
Company shall be responsible and liable for indebtedness, liabilities, expenses and other
obligations incurred in connection with activities within the proper business purposes of the
Company and as provided in Section 2.8(f).

        Section 1.7. Tax Status of Company and Subsidiaries. Notwithstanding anything in this
Agreement to the contrary, the Members intend that the Company and each of its direct and indirect
subsidiaries constitute and be treated as a partnership or “disregarded entity” for United States
federal, state and local income tax purposes and that, without approval of the Manager, no Member

                                               -2-

===== PAGE 207 =====
shall (or shall cause or permit the Company or any direct or indirect subsidiary of the Company
to), and neither the Company nor any direct or indirect subsidiary of the Company shall, either:
(a) make (or fail to make) any election and/or take (or fail to take) any action that would result in
the Company or any direct or indirect subsidiary of the Company to not constitute and be treated
as a partnership or “disregarded entity” for United States federal, state and local income tax
purposes; or (b) acquire and/or hold any interest in any Person that does not constitute either a
partnership or “disregarded entity” for United States federal, state and local tax purposes.

                                          Article II
                                     Members and Manager

       Section 2.1.    Intentionally Omitted.

       Section 2.2.    Limitation on Authority of Members.

               (a)      Except as expressly provided herein, no Member is an agent of the
Company solely by virtue of being a Member, and no Member has authority to act for the Company
solely by virtue of being a Member.

               (b)     This Section 2.2 supersedes any authority granted to the Members pursuant
to the Act. Any Member who takes any action or seeks to bind the Company in violation of this
Section 2.2 shall be solely responsible for any loss or expense incurred by the Company as a result
of the unauthorized action and shall indemnify and hold the Company harmless with respect to
such loss or expense.

        Section 2.3. Duties of Members. Nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed to restrict
in any way the rights of any Member, or of any Affiliate of any Member, to conduct any other
business or activity whatsoever, and no Member shall be accountable to the Company or to any
other Member with respect to that business or activity even if the business or activity competes
with the Company’s business. The organization of the Company shall be without prejudice to the
Members’ respective rights (or the rights of their respective Affiliates) to maintain, expand, or
diversify such other interests and activities and to receive and enjoy profits or compensation
therefrom. Each Member waives any rights the Member might otherwise have to share or
participate in such other interests or activities of any other Member or any other Member’s
Affiliates.

        Section 2.4. Members’ Expenses. When acting in the capacity of Member, no Member
(or any of its stockholders, partners, members, directors, officers, managers, agents and/or
Affiliates) shall be entitled to reimbursement for expenses incurred on behalf of the Company,
except for such expenses specifically approved by the Manager. Except with the consent of the
Manager, no Member (or any of its shareholders, partners, members, directors, officers, managers,
agents and/or Affiliates) shall, directly or indirectly, be entitled to receive any fees, salaries or
other compensation for any services rendered to or on behalf of the Company.

       Section 2.5. Appointment of Manager. The Company shall be managed by Zev
Schwartz, an individual (the “Manager”). Each of the Members agrees to approve, elect and
endorse the Manager appointed under this Section 2.5. In the event of the death, withdrawal or
                                            -3-

===== PAGE 208 =====
incapacity of the Manager, then a new Manager may be designated by the unanimous consent of
the Members.

       Section 2.6.    Powers of the Manager.

                (a)    Except for Major Decisions as described in Section 2.12 below, any matter
may be decided by the Manager without need of a meeting or the consent of the Members. Unless
otherwise restricted by the Certificate, this Agreement or the Act, the Manager shall have the
authority on behalf and in the name of the Company to take any action or make any decisions on
behalf of the Company, to carry out any and all of the purposes of the Company set forth in Section
1.4, and to perform all acts and enter into and perform all contracts and other undertakings which
it may deem necessary or advisable or incidental thereto, including, without limitation, the power
to: (i) manage and direct the business affairs of the Company, to do any and all acts on behalf of
the Company, and to exercise all rights of the Company with respect to the Company’s assets and
properties, and (ii) make such other decisions and enter into such other agreements and take such
other actions necessary or desirable to carry out the purposes of the Company. The Manager may
execute any document or take any action on behalf of the Company that has been approved by the
Manager, and such execution or action shall be binding upon the Company.

               (b)      The Company will not pay any compensation or fees to the Manager;
provided, however, the Company will reimburse the Manager for its reasonable expenses and
diligence costs in connection with the performance of its duties and obligations hereunder.

        Section 2.7. Delegation of Authority to Officers. The Manager may delegate all or any
portion of the day-to-day management and direction of the business and affairs of the Company to
officers appointed by the Manager. All officers of the Company shall serve under the Manager's
supervision. The Manager may enter into agreements with such officers relating to, among other
things, their duties, compensation and the terms under which they serve. To the extent specifically
authorized by the Manager, any officer may execute any document or take any action on behalf of
the Company, and such execution or action shall be binding upon the Company.

       Section 2.8.    Standard of Care; Indemnification.

                 (a)    To the fullest extent permitted by the Act and to such further and other
extent as is permitted by law, any and all duties (including fiduciary duties) that a Member, officer,
director, shareholder or Affiliate of a Member and the Manager or officer of the Company
(collectively, the “Covered Persons”) may otherwise have at law or in equity to the Company, to
a direct or indirect Subsidiary, to the Members, to any other Covered Person or to anyone else, are
hereby eliminated; provided, that to the extent necessary to give maximum effect to the exculpation
of Covered Persons set forth herein, nothing in this Agreement is intended to eliminate the implied
contractual covenant of good faith and fair dealing. To the fullest extent permitted by the Act and
to such further and other extent as is permitted by law, no Covered Person shall be liable to the
Company, to a direct or indirect Subsidiary, to the Members, to any other Covered Person or to
anyone else, for any breach of contract or breach of duties (including fiduciary duties) or for any
loss, damage or claim incurred by reason of any act or omission performed or omitted by such


                                                -4-

===== PAGE 209 =====
Covered Person in their capacity as such, except for acts or omissions that constitute a bad faith
violation of the implied contractual covenant of good faith and fair dealing or actual fraud.

                 (b)     To the fullest extent permitted by the Act and to such further and other
extent as is permitted by law, a Covered Person shall be indemnified and held harmless by the
Company from and against any and all claims and demands whatsoever, including for any other
liabilities eliminated in Section 2.8(a), for any threatened, pending or completed action, suit or
proceeding (whether civil, criminal, administrative or investigative) or for any other loss, damages,
judgments, reasonable settlements and expenses (including reasonable attorney’s fees) incurred by
such Covered Person by reason of any act or omission performed or omitted by the Covered Person
in his, her or its capacity as such, provided however, that the Company shall have no obligation to
indemnify a Covered Person for actions or omissions that have been determined by a court of
competent jurisdiction in a final, non-appealable order or judgment to have constituted a bad faith
violation of the implied contractual covenant of good faith and fair dealing or actual fraud.

                 (c)   To the fullest extent permitted by the Act and to such further and other
extent as is permitted by law, expenses (including reasonable legal fees) incurred by a Covered
Person in defending or investigating any claim, demand, and any threatened, pending or completed
action, suit or proceeding (whether civil, criminal, administrative or investigative) shall be
advanced by the Company, prior to the final disposition of such claim, demand, action, suit or
proceeding, from time to time and promptly upon request, after receipt by the Company of an
undertaking by or on behalf of the Covered Person to repay such amount (with no requirement to
post any collateral to secure any repayment obligation) if it shall be determined by a court of
competent jurisdiction in a final, non-appealable order or judgment, that the Covered Person is not
entitled to be indemnified as authorized in this Section 2.8. For the avoidance of doubt, a Covered
Person is entitled to advancement for expenses incurred in defending or investigating any claim
alleging that the Covered Person committed acts or omissions that constitute a bad faith violation
of the implied contractual covenant of good faith and fair dealing or actual fraud.

                (d)     In connection with any determination of entitlement to indemnification, the
Covered Person shall be presumed to be so entitled and the Company shall have the burden of
proof and persuasion to establish that the Covered Person is not so entitled. Neither the termination
of any action, suit or proceeding by judgment, order, settlement, conviction, or upon a plea of nolo
contendere or its equivalent, nor any decision by the Company shall, of itself, create a presumption
that the Covered Person is not entitled to indemnification or be in any respect binding on the
Covered Person or preclusive with respect to his, her or its rights of indemnification.

                  (e)     The Company shall also indemnify the Covered Person for any expenses
(including reasonable legal fees) that the Covered Person incurs in successfully enforcing, in whole
or in part, its rights to indemnification or advancement under this Section 2.8.

                (f)    The Company shall also indemnify the Covered Person for any expenses
(including reasonable legal fees) that the Covered Person incurs in serving as a witness, submitting
to an interview or responding to a subpoena or to a formal or informal request for documents with
respect to any claim or demand or any threatened, pending, or completed action, suit or proceeding
(whether civil, criminal, administrative or investigative) to which the Covered Person is not a party
or threatened to be made a party.
                                                 -5-

===== PAGE 210 =====
               (g)    Any indemnification or advancement under this Section 2.8 by the
Company shall be provided out of and to the extent of the Company’s assets only, and the Members
shall not have personal liability on account thereof.

                 (h)    A Covered Person shall be fully protected, shall not breach any contract or
duty (including any fiduciary duty), and shall not be held liable, in relying in good faith upon the
records of the Company and upon such information, opinions, reports or statements presented to
the Covered Person by any person as to matters the Covered Person reasonably believes are within
such other person’s professional or expert competence and who has been selected with reasonable
care by or on behalf of the Company, including without limitation, information, opinions, reports
or statements as to the financial condition and performance, the value and amount of the assets,
liabilities, profits or losses of the Company, the amount of assets or reserves or contracts,
agreements, or other undertakings that would be sufficient to pay or to make provision to pay the
claims and obligations of the Company or any other facts pertinent to the existence and amount of
assets from which distributions to the Member might properly be paid, and to such further extent
as provided under the Act.

               (i)     To the extent that, at law or in equity, a Covered Person has duties
(including fiduciary duties), and liabilities relating thereto, to the Company or to any other Covered
Person, a Covered Person acting under this Agreement shall not be liable to the Company, the
Members or to any other person bound by this Agreement for its good faith reliance on the
provisions of this Agreement.

               (j)      The provisions of this Section 2.8 to the extent that they eliminate or restrict
the duties and liabilities of a Covered Person otherwise existing at law or in equity, shall replace
such other duties and liabilities of such Covered Person.

                (k)    Rights under this Section 2.8 will not limit other rights which any Covered
Person may have by contract, under insurance policies or at law, by statute or otherwise, including
common law rights to subrogation, indemnification, reimbursement or contribution and similar
rights under applicable law. Rights of a Covered Person under this Section will survive any change
in the relationship between the Company and such Covered Person.

               (l)      The duties of the Company to indemnify and to advance expenses to
Covered Persons as provided in this Section 2.8 shall be in the nature of a contract between the
Company and each such Covered Person. A Covered Person’s rights under this Section 2.8 will
not be limited by any amendment or restatement of this Agreement, or termination of this
Agreement, after the date the Covered Person acts or refrains from taking action in reliance on
such rights, unless the Covered Person otherwise agrees. It is expressly recognized that each
Covered Person named in this Section 2.8 is a third-party beneficiary of this Agreement and may
directly enforce his, her or its rights allowed by this Section 2.8.

                (m)     The provisions of this Section 2.8 shall survive any termination of this
Agreement. Any amendment, modification or repeal of this Section 2.8 shall be prospective only
and shall not in any way affect the rights to indemnification and advancement or the limitations on
duties and liabilities established under this Section 2.8 as in effect immediately prior to such
amendment, modification or repeal with respect to claims arising from or relating to matters
                                                 -6-

===== PAGE 211 =====
occurring, in whole or in part, prior to such amendment, modification or repeal with respect to
claims arising from or relating to matters occurring, in whole or in part, prior to such amendment,
modification or repeal, regardless of when such claims may arise or be asserted.

               (n)     A Covered Person shall not be denied indemnification in whole or in part
under this Section 2.8 because the Covered Person had an interest in the transaction with respect
to which the indemnification applies if the transaction was otherwise permitted by the terms of this
Agreement or the Act.

              (o)      The Company may, if available, purchase insurance to cover losses, claims,
damages or liabilities covered by the foregoing indemnification provisions in such amount and
with such deductibles as the Manager may determine.

         Section 2.9. Other Activities. When acting in the capacity of Manager, the Manager
shall (i) devote only such of his time, as he in his sole discretion, deems reasonably necessary to
the affairs of the Company’s business and (ii) act in good faith, shall use their commercially
reasonable efforts on behalf of the Company and shall devote reasonable time and efforts to
maximize the potential of the Company’s business. The Manager and their respective Affiliates
may engage in, or possess an interest in, other business ventures of any nature and description,
independently or with others including any business which is competitive with the business of the
Company.

       Section 2.10. No Right to Partition. Except as otherwise expressly provided in this
Agreement, the Members hereby specifically renounce, waive and forfeit all rights, whether arising
under contract or statute or by operation of law, to seek, bring or maintain any action in any court
of law or equity for partition of the Company, or any interest which is considered to be Company
property, regardless of the manner in which title to any such property may be held.

       Section 2.11. Intentionally Omitted.

        Section 2.12. Major Decisions. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained
herein, neither the Manager nor any officer of the Company shall take or cause or permit the
Company or any of its Subsidiaries to take, any of the following actions, expend any amount of
money, make any decision or incur any obligation on behalf of the Company, or any Subsidiary
with respect to any matter within the scope of the matters enumerated below (each, a “Major
Decision”), unless the action, expenditure or other decision has been unanimously approved by
Members:

                (a)     Incurring, refinancing, modifying, or assuming any indebtedness, including
any line of credit, promissory note, intercompany advance, equipment loan, working capital
facility, or other borrowing, whether secured or unsecured, and whether or not in the ordinary
course of business;

               (b)   Issuing, selling, redeeming, converting, exchanging, transferring, or
otherwise disposing of any equity interests, profit interests, warrants, options, or convertible
instruments of the Company or any Subsidiary, or modifying the rights or preferences of any
existing equity;
                                             -7-

===== PAGE 212 =====
              (c)     Calling for, issuing notices of, or requiring any additional Capital
Contributions or capital calls from any Member, or amending any provision relating to Capital
Contributions or Member funding obligations.

               (d)     Selling, assigning, transferring, pledging, leasing, licensing, or otherwise
disposing of any assets of the Company or any Subsidiary, including receivables, contracts,
inventory, accounts, intellectual property, or real or personal property, whether individually or in
the aggregate;

              (e)    Amending, restating, waiving, or otherwise modifying this Agreement or
any governing or constituent documents of the Company or any Subsidiary;

                (f)    Entering into any merger, consolidation, joint venture, restructuring,
recapitalization, conversion, or similar transaction involving the Company or any Subsidiary;

                 (g)     Filing or consenting to the filing of any voluntary or involuntary
bankruptcy, insolvency, or similar debtor-relief proceeding involving the Company or any
Subsidiary; making a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; or appointing or consenting
to a receiver, trustee, or custodian;

                (h)   Forming or acquiring any new Subsidiary or business division, or entering
into any agreement (including letters of intent or term sheets) to pursue any transaction described
in this Section;

             (i)   Entering into or amending any transaction or arrangement with any Affiliate
of a Member or Manager;

             (j)    Creating, incurring, or permitting any lien, pledge, security interest, or
encumbrance on any property of the Company or any Subsidiary;

               (k)     Making any distribution, dividend, or repayment of capital;

               (l)     Taking any action, or entering into any agreement, side letter, or similar
arrangement, that has the purpose or effect of circumventing the intent or substance of this Section
2.12.

                                            Article III
                                             Capital

        Section 3.1. Capital Contributions. The Members have contributed the amounts of
capital to the Company set forth on Schedule 3.2.

         Section 3.2. Units and Unit Ratios. The Units owned by and Unit Ratios of the Members
are set forth on Schedule 3.2.

       Section 3.3. No Contribution Required. Except as otherwise specifically provided by
the Act and under the circumstances related to additional capital as provided in Section 3.4, no
Member shall be required to contribute any capital, make any other payments or lend any funds to
                                               -8-

===== PAGE 213 =====
the Company, and no Member shall have any personal liability whatsoever in such Member’s
capacity as a Member, whether to the Company, to any of the other Members, to the creditors of
the Company or to any other third party, for the debts, liabilities, commitments, expenses or other
obligations of the Company or for any losses of the Company. Neither any loan made, nor any
service performed by any Member to or for the benefit of the Company shall be deemed to
constitute a contribution to the capital of the Company for any purpose.

      Section 3.4. Additional Capital. Any further capital needs, requirements or financings
whether for working capital, capital expenditures or any other reason shall be determined
unanimously by the Members as a Major Decision.

        Section 3.5. Withdrawal of Capital: Distributions. No Member shall be entitled to the
withdrawal of such Member’s Capital Contributions, except to the extent, if any, to which
distributions made pursuant to this Agreement or upon termination or dissolution of the Company
may be considered as such by law, and then only to the extent provided in this Agreement. No
Member shall be entitled to receive any distribution from the Company, except as otherwise
expressly provided herein.

        Section 3.6. No Interest. Except as expressly provided herein, no Member shall be
entitled to interest on any Capital Contributions made to the Company.

       Section 3.7.    Capital Accounts.

                 (a)   There shall be established on the books of the Company a capital account
(“Capital Account”) for each Member. It is the intention of the Members that such Capital Account
be maintained in accordance with the provisions of Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv), and this
Agreement shall be so construed. Accordingly, such Capital Account shall initially be credited
with the agreed value of the Capital Contributions of each Member, and thereafter shall be: (a)
increased by (i) any cash or the fair market value of any additional property contributed by such
Member (net of any liabilities assumed by the Company or to which the contributed property is
subject), (ii) the amount of all net income (whether or not exempt from tax) allocated to such
Member hereunder, and (iii) to the extent not already netted out under clause (b)(ii) below, the
amount of any Company liability assumed by the Member or which is secured by any property
distributed to such Member; and (b) decreased by (i) the amount of all net losses allocated to such
Member hereunder (including expenditures described in Section 705(a)(2)(B) of the Code, or
treated as such an expenditure by reason of Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(i)), (ii) the
amount of cash, and the fair market value of property (net of any liabilities assumed by such
Member or to which the distributed property is subject) distributed to such Member pursuant to
Article VI and Section 10.2, and (iii) to the extent not already netted out under clause (a)(i) above,
the amount of any liabilities of the Member assumed by the Company or which are secured by any
property contributed by such Member to the Company.

              (b)     If any Member Transfers all or any portion of its Units or other interest in
the Company in accordance with Article IX, then the Capital Account of the transferor Member
shall become the Capital Account of the transferee to the extent of the Units transferred.


                                                -9-

===== PAGE 214 =====
                 (c)     Following the formation of the Company, and in the event of: (x) a
distribution of property which results in a change of Unit Ratios; (y) the distribution by the
Company to a Member of more than a de minimis amount of the property (other than money); or
(z) the liquidation of the Company within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(g);
then, in any such event, the book basis of the Company Property shall be adjusted to fair market
value and the Capital Accounts of all the Members shall be adjusted simultaneously to reflect the
aggregate net adjustment to book basis as if the Company recognized gain and loss equal to the
amount of such aggregate net adjustment. For purposes hereof, “Company Property” shall mean
all real and personal property acquired by the Company and any improvements thereto, and shall
include both tangible and intangible property.

                (d)    The foregoing provisions of this Section 3.7 and the other provisions of this
Agreement relating to the maintenance of capital accounts are intended to comply with Regulations
Section 1.704-1(b) and Regulations Section 1.704-2, and shall be interpreted and applied in a
manner consistent with the Regulations. In the event that the Manager determines that it is prudent
or advisable to modify the manner in which the Capital Accounts, or any increases or decreases
thereto, are computed solely in order to comply with the Regulations, the Manager may cause such
modification to be made without the consent of all of the Members; provided, however, that such
modification will not have a material effect on the amounts distributable to the Members upon the
dissolution of the Company.

       Section 3.8. Member Loans. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Article III, the
Members may make loans to the Company in such amounts, at such times, and on such terms and
conditions as may be approved by the Manager (“Member Loans”). In the event that the Manager
determines that there will be a Member Loan, each Member shall have the right to participate upon
the same terms and conditions pro rata in proportion to their respective Unit Ratios, or in the event
that some but not all of the Members elect to make Member Loans, the lending Members shall
make their Member Loans pro rata in proportion to the lending Members’ respective Unit Ratios.
Member Loans shall not be considered as contributions to the capital of the Company.

                                           Article IV
                             Allocation of Net Income and Net Loss

       Section 4.1.    Net Income.

             (a)     Subject to Sections 4.1(b) and (c), Net Cash Flow shall be allocated among
the Members at the end of each fiscal period in the following manner:

                        (i)   First, to the Members pro rata in accordance with the amount of net
       losses allocated to each such Member pursuant to Section 4.2(a)(iii) until the aggregate
       amount of net income allocated to the Members pursuant to this Section 4.1(a)(i) for such
       fiscal period and all prior fiscal periods is equal to the aggregate amount of net losses
       allocated to the Members for the current and all prior fiscal periods pursuant to Section
       4.2(a)(iii); and

                       (ii)    Second, to the Members pro rata in accordance with the amount of
       net losses allocated to each such Member pursuant to Section 4.2(a)(ii) until the aggregate
                                               - 10 -

===== PAGE 215 =====
       amount of net income allocated to the Members pursuant to this Section 4.1(a)(ii) for such
       fiscal period and all prior fiscal periods is equal to the aggregate amount of net losses
       allocated to the Members for the current and all prior fiscal periods pursuant to Section
       4.2(a)(ii); and

                       (iii) Third, to the Members pro rata in accordance with the amount of
       net losses allocated to each such Member pursuant to Section 4.2(a)(i) until the aggregate
       amount of net income allocated to the Members pursuant to this Section 4.1(a)(iii) for such
       fiscal period and all prior fiscal periods is equal to the aggregate amount of net losses
       allocated to the Members for the current and all prior fiscal periods pursuant to Section
       4.2(a)(i);

                      (iv)    Fourth, to the Members, pro rata in accordance with their respective
       negative Capital Account balances (if any), until such Capital Account balances have been
       increased to zero; and

                       (v)     Thereafter, the balance, if any, to the Members pro rata in
       proportion to their then respective Unit Ratios, as the same may be adjusted pursuant to the
       terms of this Agreement.

                (b)     If there is a net decrease in the Company’s Minimum Gain (which shall
have the same meaning as partnership minimum gain as defined in Regulations Section 1.704-
2(d)) or Partner Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain (within the meaning of Regulations Section
1.704-2(i)(3)) during any fiscal period, each Member shall be allocated, before any other
allocations hereunder, items of income and gain for such fiscal period (and subsequent fiscal
periods, if necessary), in an amount equal to such Member’s share (determined in accordance with
Regulations Sections 1.704(g)(2) and 1.704-2(i)(5), as applicable) of the net decrease in the
Company’s Minimum Gain or Partner Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain, as applicable, for such
fiscal period; provided, however, that no such allocation shall be required if any of the exceptions
set forth in Regulations Section 1.704-2(f) apply. It is the intention of the parties that the
provisions of this Section 4.1(b) constitute a “minimum gain chargeback” within the meaning of
Regulations Sections 1.704-2(f) and 1.704-2(i)(4), and such provisions shall be so construed.

                 (c)     Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, if a Member has a deficit
balance in its Capital Account (excluding from such Member’s deficit Capital Account any amount
which such Member is obligated to restore in accordance with Regulations Section 1.704-
1(b)(2)(ii)(c), as well as any amount such Member is treated as obligated to restore under
Regulations Sections 1.704-2(g)(1) and 1.704-2(i)(5)) and unexpectedly receives any adjustment,
allocation or distribution described in Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4), (5) or (6), then
such Member will be allocated items of income and gain in an amount and manner sufficient to
eliminate the deficit balance in such Member’s Capital Account as quickly as possible. If there is
an allocation to a Member pursuant to this Section 4.1(c), then any future allocations of net income
pursuant to Section 4.1 shall be adjusted so that those Members who were allocated less income
or a greater amount of loss, by reason of the allocation made pursuant to this Section 4.1(c), shall
be allocated additional net income in an equal amount. It is the intention of the parties that this
provision constitute a “qualified income offset” within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.704-
1(b)(2)(ii)(d), and this provision shall be so construed.
                                                 - 11 -

===== PAGE 216 =====
                (d)     For federal, state and local income tax purposes only, depreciation (cost
recovery) deductions and gain or loss recognized by the Company upon the sale or other
disposition of any Company Property shall be allocated so as to take into account the difference
between the agreed value of such Company Property and the Members’ adjusted basis for such
Company Property at the time of its contribution to the Company in accordance with the provisions
of Section 704(c) of the Code and the Regulations promulgated thereunder using the traditional
method (within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.704-3(b)). Notwithstanding the foregoing,
if the gain from the sale of the Company Property is being reported on the installment method for
income tax purposes, then the total amount of gain which is to be recognized by each of the
Members in accordance with the above allocations shall be computed and the amount of gain to
be recognized by each of the Members in each year shall be in proportion to the total gain to be
recognized by each of the Members in all taxable years.

       Section 4.2.   Net Loss.

                (a)     Subject to Section 4.2(b), net loss of the Company for each fiscal period
shall be allocated to the Members at the end of each fiscal period in the following manner:

                     (i)     First, to those Members with positive Capital Account balances
       (determined by taking into account the adjustments, allocations and distributions described
       in Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(a)(ii)(d)(4), (5) and (6)) in proportion to, and to the
       extent of, such Capital Account balances, until all such Member’s Capital Account
       balances have been reduced to zero; and

                     (ii)    Second, to all Members who have made Non-Recourse Loans (as
       defined in Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)) to the Company in proportion to the amounts of
       such Non-Recourse Loans; and

                       (iii) Thereafter, the balance, if any, to the Members pro rata in
       proportion to their then respective Unit Ratios, as the same may be adjusted pursuant to the
       terms of this Agreement.

                (b)    Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 4.2(a) above, no net losses shall
be allocated to a Member if such allocation would result in such Member having a deficit balance
in such Member’s Capital Account (excluding from such Member’s deficit Capital Account any
amount such Member is obligated to restore in accordance with Regulations Section 1.704-
1(b)(2)(ii)(c), as well as any amount such Member is treated as obligated to restore under
Regulations Sections 1.704-2(g)(1) and 1.704(i)(5)) unless there would be a deficit in all Members’
Capital Accounts. In such case, the net loss that would have been allocated to such Member shall
be allocated to the other Members to which such loss may be allocated without violating the
provisions of this Section 4.2(b).

               (c)     Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, the Company’s partner
nonrecourse deductions (within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(2)) shall be
allocated solely to the Member who has the economic risk of loss with respect to the partner
nonrecourse liability in accordance with the provisions of Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(1).

                                              - 12 -

===== PAGE 217 =====
        Section 4.3. Allocations Upon Transfers. In the event of the Transfer of all or any part
of a Member’s Units pursuant to Article IX or otherwise in accordance with the provisions of this
Agreement or the admission of a new Member at any time other than at the end of a Fiscal Year,
then the distributive share of the transferring Member, transferee Member, or new Member of the
Company’s net income, gain, net loss, deductions and credits, as computed both for accounting
purposes and for federal income tax purposes, shall be allocated between the transferor Member
and the transferee Member, or among the new Member and the other Members, as the case may
be, in the same ratio as the number of days in such Fiscal Year before and after the date of such
Transfer or admission, provided, however, that the Members shall have the option to treat the
periods before and after the date of such Transfer or admission as separate Fiscal Years and allocate
the Company’s net income, gain, net loss, deductions and credits for each of such deemed separate
Fiscal Years in accordance with the Members’ respective interests in the Company for such
deemed separate Fiscal Years. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if, the Company uses the cash
receipts and disbursements method of accounting, the Company’s “allocable cash basis items,” as
that term is used in Section 706(d)(2)(B) of the Code, shall be allocated as required by Section
706(d)(2) of the Code and the Regulations promulgated thereunder.

         Section 4.4. Allocation of Excess Nonrecourse Liabilities. For purposes of Section 752
of the Code and the Regulations thereunder, the excess nonrecourse liabilities of the Company
(within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.752-3(a)(3)), if any, shall be allocated to the
Members in accordance with their respective Unit Ratios, as the same may be adjusted pursuant
to the terms of this Agreement.



                                          Article V
                      Allocable Shares and Federal Income Tax Elections

        Section 5.1. Allocable Shares. For purposes of Subchapter K of the Code, the
distributive shares of the Members of each item of Company taxable income, gain, loss, deduction
or credit for any fiscal period shall be in the same proportions as their respective shares of the
items allocated to them pursuant to Sections 4.1 and 4.2. Notwithstanding the foregoing, to the
extent not inconsistent with the allocation of gain provided for in Section 4.1, gain recognized by
the Company which represents ordinary income by reason of recapture of depreciation or cost
recovery deductions for federal income tax purposes shall be allocated to the Member (or the
Member’s successor-in-interest) to whom such depreciation or cost recovery deduction to which
such recapture relates was allocated.

       Section 5.2. Elections. The election permitted to be made by Section 754 of the Code,
and any other elections required or permitted to be made by the Company under the Code, shall
be made as the Members or the Partnership Representative (as hereinafter defined) shall determine.




                                               - 13 -

===== PAGE 218 =====
                                          Article VI
                              Return of Capital and Distributions

       Section 6.1. Distributions. At such times as the Members shall reasonably determine by
Major Decision, the Company shall distribute such funds to the Members as the Members deem
appropriate when available in the following order of priority:

                      (i)  First, to the Members pro rata in proportion to their respective
       Unpaid Preferred Return, until the Unpaid Preferred Return of each Member has been
       reduced to zero;

                    (ii)   Second, to the Members pro rata in proportion to their respective
       Unreturned Capital Contributions, until the Unreturned Capital Contribution of each
       Member has been reduced to zero; and

                      (iii) Thereafter, to all Members, pro rata, in proportion to their
       respective Unit Ratios.

         Section 6.2. Tax Distributions. To the extent the Company has Net Cash Flow, the
Company will distribute to the Members, pro rata in proportion to their respective Unit Ratios, as
the same may be adjusted pursuant to the terms of this Agreement, (i) within ninety (90) days of
the end of each of the Company’s Fiscal Years or as soon as reasonably practical after the receipt
of the Fiscal Year financial statements for the Company and its Subsidiaries, an aggregate amount
estimated to be large enough so that there is distributed to each Member an amount at least equal
to the Maximum Effective Tax Rate multiplied by the excess (if any) of (a) the total cumulative
amount of taxable income (which, for the avoidance of doubt, taxable income is computed after
deducting for all guaranteed payments) and gain allocated to such Member from the inception of
the Company through the end of such Fiscal Year, over (b) the total cumulative amount of taxable
loss and deduction allocated to such Member from the inception of the Company through the end
of such Fiscal Year; over (ii) the total cumulative tax distributions made to such Member from the
inception of the Company under this Section 6.2. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the amount of
taxable income allocable to the Members for a Fiscal Year would, when combined with all other
allocations of income or loss from the Company since its formation, create an aggregate taxable
loss for the Company, then the Company shall not make such distribution for that Fiscal Year.
Amounts otherwise distributable to a Member pursuant to Section 6.1, Section 6.4 and Section
10.2 shall be reduced by all distributions to such Member pursuant to this Section 6.2. For the
purposes of this Section 6.2, “Maximum Effective Tax Rate” means the maximum effective tax
rate in effect for the Member (or the taxpaying direct or indirect owner of an interest in a Member
which is an S corporation or an entity treated as a partnership for federal income tax purposes)
with the highest federal and state income tax brackets for the Fiscal Year (with a proper adjustment
for (i) the deductibility of state income taxes on federal income tax returns, and (ii) tax credits,
capital gains and losses, and other specially allocated items which pass through to a Member based
on Units owned and taking into account any additional federal taxes likely to be imposed under
Section 1411 of the Code). Each Member will furnish the Manager with such information as may
reasonably be requested to determine the Maximum Effective Tax Rate. For purposes of this


                                               - 14 -

===== PAGE 219 =====
definition, “Member” shall include a Member’s transferor or other predecessor in interest. The
foregoing shall be appropriately adjusted to reflect changes in tax rates and law.

       Section 6.3. Withholding on a Member’s Distributable Share. Notwithstanding
anything contained in this Agreement to the contrary, distributions to a Member pursuant to
Sections 6.1 and 10.2 will be reduced by any and all amounts which are withheld by the Company
and remitted to any federal, state or local tax agency on behalf of such Member.

        Section 6.4. Property Distributions. If any property of the Company, other than cash, is
distributed by the Company to any Member(s) in connection with the liquidation of the Company
or otherwise, the fair market value of such property shall be used for purposes of determining the
amount of such distribution. The difference, if any, of such fair market value over (or under) the
value at which such property is carried on the books of the Company shall be credited or charged
to the Capital Accounts of the Members in proportion to the ratio in which the Members share in
the gain and loss of the Company pursuant to Sections 4.1 and 4.2, respectively. The fair market
value of the property distributed shall be agreed to in good faith by the Manager.

                                        Article VII
                           Books and Records; Accounting; Reports

       Section 7.1. Books and Records. The Manager shall maintain the Company’s books and
records at the Company’s principal place of business, showing all receipts and expenditures, assets
and liabilities, profits and losses, and all other records necessary for recording the Company’s
business and affairs. The Company’s books and records shall be maintained, and the net income
and net loss of the Company shall be determined, in accordance with generally accepted
accounting principles. Each Member, at its sole cost and expense, shall have the right, personally
or by an independent certified public accountant of its own choosing, to examine such books and
records at the Company’s principal offices during regular business hours, and to make copies
and/or excerpts therefrom.

       Section 7.2.    Fiscal Year. The fiscal year of the Company shall end on December 31
(“Fiscal Year”).

        Section 7.3.   Reports. The Company shall distribute to each Member the following
reports:

               (a)    not later than one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each Fiscal
Year an unaudited balance sheet and unaudited statements of income and cash flows for the
Company fairly presenting the financial position and results of operations of the Company at and
for such Fiscal Year;

                (b)    not later than sixty (60) days after the end of each fiscal quarter unaudited
statements of income for the Company fairly presenting the results of operations of the Company
for such fiscal quarter, together with calculations of EBITDAR and an occupancy report, which
shall be prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles;


                                               - 15 -

===== PAGE 220 =====
                (c)   not later than sixty (60) days after the end of each month unaudited
statements of income for the Company fairly presenting the results of operations of the Company
for such month, which shall be prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting
principles; and

               (d)     from time to time upon request of any Member in writing such other
financial information as such Member may reasonably request.

        Section 7.4. Tax Returns and Other Reports. Within one hundred twenty (120) days
after the close of each Fiscal Year of the Company, the Company shall furnish to each Member all
such information relating to the Company which shall be necessary for the preparation by the
Members of their federal and state income or other tax returns. The Company shall prepare, or
cause to be prepared, and file or cause to be filed on or before the due date (including extensions),
all federal, state and local income tax returns and information returns, if any, which the Company
is required to file. The Company shall prepare and file with appropriate state authorities any
reports required to be filed by it with such authorities. All expenses incurred in connection with
such tax returns and reports, as well as all reports set forth in this Article VII, shall be at the sole
cost and expense of the Company.

                                            Article VIII
                                           Bank Accounts

        Section 8.1. Bank Accounts. All funds of the Company shall be deposited in its name
in one or more separate checking and savings accounts, cash equivalent accounts and/or in short-
term investments as shall be designated by the Manager or by the Company’s lender, as the case
may be. The funds in the Company’s account shall be used solely for the business of the Company
and to make the payments and distributions to the Members provided for in this Agreement. Funds
belonging to the Company shall not be commingled with those of any other Person.

        Section 8.2. Withdrawals. Withdrawals from the Company’s accounts shall be made
only upon the signature of such Person or Persons as may be designated by the Manager from time
to time. All checks of the Company shall be signed by such Person(s) as shall from time to time
be designated by the Manager.

                                             Article IX
                                          Transfer of Units

        Section 9.1. Restrictions. Except as set forth in Section 9.2 and subject to compliance
with the requirements of Section 9.3, no Member may Transfer all or any part of such Member’s
Units (including any economic interest therein), except with the written consent of the Manager.
Any purported Transfer of a Member’s Units in violation of the terms of this Agreement shall be
null and void and without any effect. Each Member shall communicate to the other Members the
terms of any offer which it may receive for the purchase of any asset or properties of the Company.

       Section 9.2. Permitted Transfers. The requirements of this Article IX (other than Section
9.3, which shall apply to every Transfer of Units) shall not apply to the following Transfers (each

                                                 - 16 -

===== PAGE 221 =====
of which shall be deemed to constitute a “Permitted Transfer,” and each transferee of a Permitted
Transfer is referred to herein as a “Permitted Transferee”):

                       (i)     a Transfer approved in writing by the Manager;

                      (ii)    in a liquidation, wind-down or dissolution of a Member only, a
       Transfer by a Member to an Affiliate of such Member or to all of the partners, members,
       shareholders or other equity owners of such Member;

                      (iii) with respect to an individual Member or the beneficial owner(s) of
       a Member that is an entity, (w) pursuant to applicable laws of descent and distribution, (x)
       to such Member’s or its beneficial owner’s spouse, former spouse, siblings, children,
       grandchildren or other relatives, (y) to the trustee, fiduciary or personal representative of
       any Member or its beneficial owner and any trust solely for the benefit of a Member or
       such Member’s relatives or its beneficial owner, or (z) to any limited partnership, limited
       liability company, corporation or other entity the governing instruments of which provide
       that such Member or its beneficial owner shall have the exclusive, nontransferable power
       to direct management and policies of such entity and of which the sole owners are limited
       to the Member or its beneficial owner and the Member’s or its beneficial owner’s relatives;
       and

                      (iv)    for the benefit of the Company’s lenders only, any mortgage, pledge
       or grant of a security interest by a Member in the Units held by such Member or of any
       ownership interest in a Member.

         Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein, (i) the sale or the making of a
gift of all or part of an individual Member’s Units in or to trust for the benefit of members of his
or her immediate family or to an Affiliate; or (ii) upon the death of any individual Member, any
Transfer of such equity interest owned by such Member to or from his or her executors,
administrators or legal representatives only, shall, in either case, be a permitted Transfer hereunder
and shall not be subject to the restrictions set forth in this Article IX, provided that the transferee
has no right to become a substituted Member unless the transferee complies with Sections 9.3(a)
and (b).

       Section 9.3.    Substitute Members.

             (a)    No transferee of all or part of a Member’s Units in accordance with this
Agreement shall become a “Substitute Member” in lieu of the transferor Member unless and until:

                     (i)   the transferor Member has stated such intention in an instrument of
       assignment and assumption in form reasonably satisfactory to the Manager;

                     (ii)    the transferee has delivered an executed counterpart of this
       Agreement as a Member, and executed originals of such other documents as may be
       required by applicable law or reasonably required by the Members;



                                                - 17 -

===== PAGE 222 =====
                     (iii) the transferor Member and/or transferee has paid all costs and
       expenses of the Company, including without limitation, reasonable attorneys’ fees, in
       connection with the admission of the transferee as a Substitute Member; and

                   (iv)     pre-Transfer approval has been obtained, if necessary, by any
       Company lender, if required.

              (b)     The Manager shall cause Schedule 3.2 to this Agreement to be duly
amended to reflect the admission of such transferee as a Substitute Member.

        Section 9.4. Effect of Admission as a Substitute Member. Unless and until admitted as
a Substitute Member pursuant to Section 9.3 above, a Permitted Transferee of a Member’s Units
shall not be entitled to exercise any rights of a Member in the Company, including the right to
vote, grant approvals or give consents with respect to such Units, the right to require any
information or accounting of the Company’s business or the right to inspect the Company’s books
and records, but such transferee shall be entitled to receive, to the extent of the Units transferred
to such transferee, the distributions to which the transferor Member would otherwise be entitled.
A transferee who has become a Substitute Member has, to the extent of the Units transferred to
such transferee, all the rights and powers of the Member for whom it is substituted and is subject
to the restrictions and liabilities of a Member under this Agreement and the Act. Upon admission
of a transferee as a Substitute Member as set forth herein, the transferor of the Units so acquired
by the Substitute Member shall cease to be a Member of the Company to the extent of the interest
represented by such Units. A Person shall not cease to be a Member upon assignment of all or any
portion of its Units unless and until each transferee becomes a Substitute Member pursuant to the
terms hereof.

        Section 9.5. Withdrawal, Retirement or Resignation of a Member. No Member shall
have the right or power, or shall attempt, to withdraw, resign or retire from the Company as a
Member or demand or seek the return of any Capital Contribution or Capital Account balance prior
to the specific date set forth in the Certificate for the expiration of the term of the Company or
pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. Any act or purported act of a Member in violation of this
Section 9.4 shall be null and void and of no effect.

       Section 9.6. Costs. All reasonable costs and expenses incurred by any Member in
connection with a Transfer hereunder, including all attorneys’ fees, costs and disbursements and
any finders’ fees or brokerage commissions shall be borne by the Member who originally initiated
the Transfer pursuant to this Article IX.

        Section 9.7. Closings. At any closing for the purchase of Units, such Units shall be free
and clear of any liens, claims, options, charges, encumbrances or rights (other than those arising
hereunder), and the selling Member shall so represent and warrant, and the selling Member shall
further represent that it is the beneficial and record owner of such Units and has the authority to
Transfer such Units. At such closing, each purchaser of Units shall deliver at such closing payment
for the cash portion of the consideration for the Units purchased by it by certified or official bank
check or wire transfer and shall pay the balance in accordance with the agreed upon terms. At


                                               - 18 -

===== PAGE 223 =====
such closing, all of the parties shall execute such additional documents as are otherwise customary
and appropriate.

        Section 9.8. Damages. If a Member resigns or withdraws from the Company or
Transfers or pledges or otherwise encumbers all or any portion of its Units in violation of the
provisions of this Article IX, or voluntarily liquidates, dissolves or suffers an act of bankruptcy,
such Member shall remain liable for any debts, obligations and liabilities of the Company assumed
by such Member pursuant to this Agreement or under the Act to the same extent as if such act had
not occurred. In addition, any resignation, withdrawal, Transfer, pledge or other encumbrance in
violation of any provision of this Article IX or any voluntary liquidation, dissolution or act of
bankruptcy of a Member, shall render the defaulting party liable to the Member and the other
Members for any damages sustained by reason of such act.

        Section 9.9. To Whom Distributions May Be Made. Unless named in this Agreement,
or unless admitted to the Company as a Member as provided in this Agreement, no Person shall
be considered a Member. The Company and any Member need deal only with Persons so named
or admitted as Members, and shall not be required to deal with any other Person merely because
of an assignment or Transfer of a Member’s Units to such Person as a result of an assignment
thereof or by reason of the death, incompetence or bankruptcy of a Member, or for any other
reason; provided, however, that any distribution by the Company to any Person shown on the
Company records as a Member, or to its legal representatives or successors, shall acquit the
Company and the Members of all liability to any other Person which may be interested in such
distribution by reason of any assignment by such Member or by reason of its death, incompetence
or bankruptcy or for any other reason. Nothing herein, however, shall confer any rights upon any
assignee to which such assignee was not otherwise entitled by law or under this Agreement.

        Section 9.10. Bankruptcy. For purposes of this Agreement, the term “bankruptcy” shall
refer to a situation where a Member shall: (a) be adjudicated a bankrupt, (b) suffer or permit a
receiver to be appointed to hold or administer any substantial portion of its assets and such
appointment shall remain in effect for sixty (60) days, (c) make an assignment for the benefit of
its creditors, or (d) file a petition for an arrangement with its creditors or an involuntary proceeding
under the provisions of the federal Bankruptcy Code or any state statute for the relief of debtors.

                                              Article X
                                    Dissolution and Liquidation

       Section 10.1. Events Causing Dissolution. The Company shall be dissolved and wound
up upon the occurrence of any of the following events:

               (a)     the written agreement of all Members;

               (b)      a merger or consolidation or similar event of the Company in which the
Company is not the surviving entity or as a result of which the Members do not retain a majority
of the voting power in the surviving entity, or a sale or other disposition or series of sales or other
dispositions of all or substantially all of the Company’s assets or properties; or


                                                 - 19 -

===== PAGE 224 =====
               (c)     any other event requiring the dissolution and winding up of the Company
under the laws of the State of New Jersey.

        Section 10.2. Liquidation. Upon dissolution of the Company, a Member or other person
selected by the Members (“Liquidator”) shall (i) within a reasonable time cause the Company
assets to be liquidated in an orderly and business-like manner in the sole reasonable discretion of
the Liquidator, and (ii) take the following actions and make the following distributions out of the
assets of the Company in the following manner and order:

                (a)     first, pay or make appropriate provision for all Third Party Loans and other
debts and liabilities of the Company to Persons other than Members and expenses of liquidation
in the order of priority provided by law;

               (b)    second, establish any reserves which the Liquidator deems reasonably
necessary or advisable to provide for any contingent or unforeseen liabilities or obligations of the
Company;

            (c)   third, pay or make appropriate provision for all debts and liabilities of the
Company to Members and to pay Member Loans;

                (d)      thereafter, make distributions to the Members in the order of priority set
forth in Section 6.1(i).

       Except as otherwise expressly provided herein, upon such distribution, no Member shall
have any rights or claims against the Company or any other Member, notwithstanding any
imbalance in the respective Capital Accounts of the Members.

        Section 10.3. Certain Obligations. No Member shall have any obligation to restore any
deficit balance in its Capital Account following the “liquidation” (as such term is defined in
Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(g)) of its interest in the Company.

        Section 10.4. Distribution in Kind. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 10.2, if, on
dissolution of the Company, the Liquidator shall determine that the sale of part or all of the
Company’s assets would cause undue loss to the Members, the Liquidator may, in order to avoid
such losses, either:

              (a)     defer the liquidation of, and withhold from distribution for a reasonable
time, any assets of the Company, except those necessary to satisfy debts and liabilities of the
Company (other than those to Members); or

               (b)    distribute to the Members, in lieu of cash, interests in any Company assets
and liquidate only such assets as are necessary in order to pay the debts and liabilities of the
Company.

        Section 10.5. Income and Loss During Liquidation. The Members shall continue to share
allocations of net income and losses during the period of liquidation in accordance with Article
IV. Any gain or loss realized by the Company upon the sale of its property shall be deemed
recognized and allocated to the Members in the manner set forth in Article IV. To the extent that
                                             - 20 -

===== PAGE 225 =====
an asset is to be distributed in kind, such asset shall be deemed to have been sold at its fair market
value of the date of distribution, the gain or loss deemed realized upon such deemed sale shall be
allocated in accordance with Article IV and the amount of the distribution shall be considered the
fair market value of the asset.



                                           Article XI
                                   Investment Representations

        Section 11.1. No Registration. Each Member acknowledges that, pursuant to exemptions
from registration requirements, the Units have not been and will not be registered with the
Securities and Exchange Commission or the securities commission of any state and that,
accordingly, the Units may not be resold or otherwise transferred except in compliance with
applicable federal and state securities laws.

         Section 11.2. Economic Risk. Each Member represents to the Company that: (i) it is
acquiring the Units for investment purposes only and not with a view to their resale or distribution;
(ii) it can bear the economic risk of losing its entire investment in the Company; (iii) its overall
commitment to investments, which are not readily marketable is not disproportionate to its net
worth, and its acquisition of the Units will not cause such overall commitment to become
disproportionate; and (iv) it has adequate means of providing for its current needs and personal
contingencies and has no need for liquidity in its investment in the Units.

       Section 11.3. Advice of Counsel. Each Member acknowledges that the Company has
advised and urged each Member in writing to consult with its own tax, legal and financial advisors
regarding its individual circumstances and the suitability of an investment in the Company. Each
Member has had such opportunity as it considers adequate to ask questions of and receive answers
from representatives of the Company concerning the Company, and to obtain from representatives
of the Company such information which the Company possesses or can acquire without
unreasonable effort or expense, as is necessary to evaluate the merits and risks of an investment in
the Company.

                                     Miscellaneous Provisions

       Section 12.1. Amendments.

               (a)   Except as expressly otherwise provided in this Agreement, any amendments
to this Agreement shall be proposed by the Manager and adopted with the unanimous written
consent of the Members.

               (b)    All consents or approvals required in connection with this Agreement may
be delivered by electronic mail confirmation in lieu of delivery of an actual signature and, when

pages added to this Agreement.
